indication.text: Treatment of adults with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) caused by susceptible microorganisms including S. pneumoniae, S. aureus (methicillin-susceptible), H. influenzae, L. pneumophila, M. pneumoniae, and C. pneumoniae.

citations.quote: XENLETA is a pleuromutilin antibacterial indicated for the treatment of adults with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) caused by susceptible microorganisms. (1.1)

XENLETA is indicated for the treatment of adults with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) caused by the following susceptible microorganisms: *Streptococcus pneumoniae*, *Staphylococcus aureus* (methicillin-susceptible isolates), *Haemophilus influenzae*, *Legionella pneumophila*, *Mycoplasma pneumoniae*, and *Chlamydomphila pneumoniae*.

target_moa.text: Lefamulin is a pleuromutilin antibacterial that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding the peptidyl transferase center (PTC) at the 50S subunit of the bacterial ribosome; mammalian protein synthesis appears unaffected.

citations.quote: The mechanism of action studies support that lefamulin is a member of the pleuromutilin class of antibacterials. Lefamulin inhibits prokaryotic ribosomal protein synthesis by binding to the peptidyl transferase center (PTC) at the 50S subunit of the bacterial ribosome, while mammalian protein synthesis appears to be unaffected.
Lefamulin (XENLETA) is a pleuromutilin antibacterial drug available as oral and IV formulations.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥2%): for XENLETA Injection administration site reactions (7%), hepatic enzyme elevation, nausea, hypokalemia, insomnia, headache; for XENLETA Tablets diarrhea (12% vs 1% moxifloxacin), nausea (5%), vomiting (3%), hepatic enzyme elevation. Warnings include QT prolongation and embryo-fetal toxicity.
